title: Conditional descent of native adic finiteness from affine schemes
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, an algebraic closure $\Omega$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure], with the absolute-value topology extending that of each finite subextension [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], and an algebraically closed field $K$ with $\operatorname{char}K\ne\ell$. For every $K$-scheme $V$, on a small representative of its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], let $B_V$ be the sheaf whose sections over $W\to V$ are continuous functions $|W|\to\Omega$ whose values locally span a finite-dimensional $\mathbf Q_\ell$-vector space. Let $\mathcal A(V)=\operatorname{Mod}(B_V)$ be the category of sheaves of modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Call an object constructible if Zariski locally it has a finite partition by locally closed constructible subschemes [def-weil-locally-closed-subset, def-weil-constructible-subset] on each of which it is pro-etale locally isomorphic to $B^{\oplus r}$, for a finite rank $r$ allowed to depend on the covering member. Write $D^b_c(\mathcal A(V))$ for objects of the ordinary derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] with cohomology zero outside a finite integer interval and constructible in every degree. For a scheme morphism $g:X\to Y$, let $g_*:\mathcal A(X)\to\mathcal A(Y)$ be the ordinary sheaf direct image, with its $B_Y$-action given by precomposition of functions $B_Y\to g_*B_X$, and let $Rg_*$ be its total right derived functor [def-sfb-right-derived-functor].

Assume the following affine hypothesis for this $K$ and $\ell$: for every affine $K$-scheme $Y$ locally of finite type over $K$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], every affine scheme $X$, every locally finite-type morphism $g:X\to Y$, and every constructible $M\in\mathcal A(X)$, one has $Rg_*(M[0])\in D^b_c(\mathcal A(Y))$.

Then for every quasi-compact, quasi-separated [def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism], locally finite-type morphism $f:X\to Y$ with $Y$ quasi-compact and locally of finite type over $K$, the actual derived direct image satisfies
$$Rf_*(L)\in D^b_c(\mathcal A(Y))\qquad\text{for every }L\in D^b_c(\mathcal A(X)).$$

proof.text: First establish the ambient facts without invoking any affine finiteness theorem. The field $K$ is Noetherian (its only ideals are zero and the whole ring), so $\operatorname{Spec}K$ is locally Noetherian. By [pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft], $Y$ is locally Noetherian. On the small site chosen in the statement, [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist] applies to the commutative ring sheaf $B_T$: $\mathcal A(T)$ is Grothendieck abelian and has K-injective resolutions, for every scheme $T$. Direct image of module sheaves is additive and left exact: its sectionwise definition preserves addition, finite products and kernels. Consequently [lem-pc-right-derived-functor-triangulated] makes $Rg_*$ triangulated for every $g:T\to Y$. The bounded constructible subcategory of the target is triangulated by [lem-sf-native-adic-bounded-constructible-triangulated]. In the following, $P(g)$ means that $Rg_*$ sends every object of $D^b_c(\mathcal A(T))$ into $D^b_c(\mathcal A(Y))$.

source.place: Devissage, finiteLowerStar and its IsTriangulated instance (94-115); field/noetherian application as in finiteFor_of_isAffine (444).

proof.text: A sheaf-level finiteness assertion for a fixed $g$ implies $P(g)$. Indeed, let $C$ have cohomology in $[a,b]$. The canonical truncation triangle [lem-weil-pbc-truncation-triangle] has terms $\tau_{\le q-1}C$, $\tau_{\le q}C$, $H^q(C)[-q]$. By [lem-weil-pbc-truncation-cohomology], $\tau_{\le a-1}C\cong0$ and $\tau_{\le b}C\cong C$: the displayed maps induce isomorphisms on every cohomology sheaf. The sheaf hypothesis puts $Rg_*(H^q(C)[0])$ in $D^b_c$, and step 1 puts its shift $Rg_*(H^q(C)[-q])$ there too. Apply $Rg_*$ to these triangles and induct from $q=a$ to $b$; two-out-of-three puts $Rg_*C$ in $D^b_c$. The zero complex is the empty-interval case. In particular, if $Y$ and $T$ are affine and $g:T\to Y$ is locally of finite type, the affine hypothesis in the statement gives $P(g)$.

source.place: finiteLowerStar_of_bounded (142-148), applied conditionally to the affine hypothesis.

proof.text: For an open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow T$, [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization](1) identifies $U_{\mathrm{proet}}$ with the localized site $T_{\mathrm{proet}}/U$, and under it $B_T|_U=B_U$: both have as sections over $W\to U$ the locally finite continuous functions on the same space $|W|$, with the same restrictions. Restriction of module sheaves to this slice is exact by [lem-sfb-ringed-site-restriction-kflat]; an exact functor preserves kernels, images and quotients, so $H^n(C|_U)\cong H^n(C)|_U$ for every complex $C$ and every $n$. Since $j^{-1}B_T=B_U$, the module pullback $B_U\otimes_{j^{-1}B_T}j^{-1}M$ of [lem-sf-native-adic-constructible-pullback] is $M|_U$, so that node makes every $H^n(C)|_U$ constructible; vanishing outside an interval is kept. Thus restriction preserves bounded constructible complexes. Suppose $T=U\cup V$ and $P(g|_U)$, $P(g|_V)$ and $P(g|_{U\cap V})$ hold. For each $C\in D^b_c(\mathcal A(T))$, apply [lem-sf-native-adic-mayer-vietoris-triangle]. Its middle term is a finite sum of bounded constructible objects, and its third term is bounded constructible. Triangulated closure from step 1 therefore puts its first term $Rg_*C$ in $D^b_c$. This proves $P(g)$. For $T=\varnothing$, the only object of $T_{\mathrm{proet}}$ is $\varnothing$, covered by the empty family, so the sheaf condition makes every module sheaf, and hence every complex, zero; $P(g)$ holds as well.

We will use step 3 in the following explicit finite induction. Fix $g:T\to Y$ and a class $\mathscr P$ of opens of $T$ closed under binary intersections. Suppose $P(g|_O)$ holds for every $O\in\mathscr P$. Claim: it holds on every finite union of members of $\mathscr P$. Induct strongly on the number $n$ of opens. For $n=0$ use the empty-source case of step 3. For $n>0$, write the union as $O_1\cup V$, with $V=\bigcup_{i=2}^n O_i$. The induction hypothesis gives $P(g|_V)$. Its overlap with $O_1$ equals $\bigcup_{i=2}^n(O_1\cap O_i)$, a union of at most $n-1$ members of $\mathscr P$, so the same induction hypothesis gives $P$ on that overlap. Step 3 then gives $P$ on the original union. Repeated or empty members do not change this argument. This is just finite induction using the cited two-open triangle, not a new finiteness input.

Now fix an affine target $Y$ and a quasi-compact quasi-separated locally finite-type $g:T\to Y$. The source $T$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-over-affine]. Whenever $O\subseteq T$ is quasi-compact open, its inclusion is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](1), hence finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-qc-open-immersion-finite-type]; composing with $g$ remains finite type by [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change]. In particular all affine open restrictions of $g$ satisfy the affine hypothesis of step 2. Suppose $O$ is quasi-compact and contained in an affine open $A$ of $T$. Cover $O$ by finitely many affine opens using [lem-pqf-finite-affine-cover-qc-open]. All their binary intersections, and all further finite intersections, are affine: apply [lem-weil-pbc-affine-source-morphism-separated] to $A\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$, then [lem-weil-pbc-separated-affine-open-intersection] to affine opens of $A$. The class of affine opens of $A$ contained in $O$ is therefore intersection-closed, and step 2 gives $P$ on each of them. Step 4 gives $P(g|_O)$.

proof.text: For this same $T$, take $\mathscr P$ to be the quasi-compact opens contained in some affine open of $T$. This class is closed under intersections. To check the quasi-compactness assertion explicitly, cover $O,O'\in\mathscr P$ by finite affine families using [lem-pqf-finite-affine-cover-qc-open]. Every pairwise intersection of members of these two covers is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-separated-affine-cover-criterion](1), since $T$ is quasi-separated. Their finite union is $O\cap O'$, so it is quasi-compact (each open cover has a finite subcover on each of the finitely many pieces). Moreover $O\cap O'$ is still contained in the affine open containing $O$. Step 5 proves $P$ on every member of $\mathscr P$. Finally [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-finite-affine-open-cover] covers $T$ by finitely many affine opens, each belonging to $\mathscr P$. Step 4 proves $P(g)$ on $T$. No intersection of arbitrary affine opens of $T$ has been asserted affine.

proof.text: Return to the given $f:X\to Y$ and $L\in D^b_c(\mathcal A(X))$. The quasi-compact scheme $Y$ has a finite affine open cover $Y=\bigcup_{i=1}^r V_i$ by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-finite-affine-open-cover]. Put $X_i=X\times_YV_i=f^{-1}(V_i)$, with open inclusion $j_i:X_i\hookrightarrow X$ and projection $f_i:X_i\to V_i$. The morphism $f$ is finite type by definition; [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change](2) makes $f_i$ finite type, and [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](3) preserves its quasi-separatedness. Each $V_i$ is locally finite type over $K$, by restriction of the local finite-type condition to an open subscheme. Step 6 therefore applies to $f_i$. By step 3, restriction and [lem-sf-native-adic-constructible-pullback] give $j_i^*L\in D^b_c(\mathcal A(X_i))$. Hence $R(f_i)_*j_i^*L\in D^b_c(\mathcal A(V_i))$. Now apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-derived-slice-localization] to the morphism of ringed sites defined by $f$: the continuous functor $u:Y_{\mathrm{proet}}\to X_{\mathrm{proet}}$, $W\mapsto W\times_YX$, with the precomposition ring map $B_Y\to f_*B_X$ of the statement, and to the object $V_i$ of $Y_{\mathrm{proet}}$, for which $u(V_i)=X_i$. It gives $j_{V_i}^*Rf_*L\cong R(f_{V_i})_*j_{X_i}^*L$, where $f_{V_i}$ is the localized morphism $X_{\mathrm{proet}}/X_i\to Y_{\mathrm{proet}}/V_i$ with the restricted ring map. Under the identifications of [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization](1) of these two slices with $(X_i)_{\mathrm{proet}}$ and $(V_i)_{\mathrm{proet}}$, with $B_X|_{X_i}=B_{X_i}$ and $B_Y|_{V_i}=B_{V_i}$ as in step 3, the localized functor sends $W\to V_i$ to $W\times_YX=W\times_{V_i}X_i\to X_i$, which is the functor defining $f_i$, and the restricted ring map is the precomposition map $B_{V_i}\to f_{i*}B_{X_i}$. Hence $(Rf_*L)|_{V_i}\cong R(f_i)_*j_i^*L$ in $D(\mathcal A(V_i))$, including the coefficient action defined by precomposition.

proof.text: Write $C=Rf_*L$. By the exactness of restriction used in step 3, $H^n(C)|_{V_i}\cong H^n(C|_{V_i})$, which is constructible by step 7. Constructibility is Zariski local by its definition in the statement: for any point choose a member $V_i$ containing it, then a neighbourhood and finite partition witnessing constructibility there; that neighbourhood is also open in $Y$. Thus every $H^n(C)$ is constructible. For each $i$ choose integers $a_i\le b_i$ outside which $H^n(C|_{V_i})=0$. If the finite cover is nonempty, put $a=\min_i a_i$ and $b=\max_i b_i$. For $n<a$ or $n>b$, the sheaf $F=H^n(C)$ restricts to zero on every $V_i$. For any object $W\to Y$ of $Y_{\mathrm{proet}}$, the open immersions $W\times_YV_i\to W$ form a Zariski open cover of $W$, hence a pro-etale covering [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], and $F(W\times_YV_i)=F|_{V_i}(W\times_YV_i\to V_i)=0$; the sheaf condition embeds $F(W)$ into the product of these zero groups, so $F=0$. If $Y$ is empty, $\mathcal A(Y)$ is zero as in step 3 and any finite interval works. Therefore $C$ is bounded with constructible cohomology, which is precisely the conclusion.
